title: The Stone in the Loft

arc.title: The Cold Stone
arc.subtitle: a warm stone, already going cold

epigraph.text: What a house keeps where nobody looks, it keeps without an account: the stone in the loft, the sixth where no thumb can reach it, the fire's fifth that never comes. Ask the pot. The pot has been told.
epigraph.attribution: A saying of the Vail kiln-house, in the second week of Ember

pov: Daniel Marchetti (Corin), close third-person past tense inside a one-hundred-and-eighty-three-to-one-hundred-and-eighty-five-day-old body carried everywhere and told by nobody --- six months and three days to six months and five days, no roof with a word for it. The surgeon's register colours the noticing (the week's ordinary tending as a theatre kept behind a screen and a gate of two bites, the carrying arm as a record in muscle that keeps weight and not cost, the private file turned out as instruments laid on a towel, a debt held at the teeth as a chart closed over its finding with the neat margin showing, the stone taken from its pot and put back as a thing looked at once and not reconciled, likenesses taken down one at a time) without a present-tense Chicago break or a tagged remembered line --- the old life stays offstage --- and there is no departure from his eyes, no Court, collector or back-room interior, no market, no Cross and no Account-day in these days, no Berr, Hessa, soft-cuffed clerk, green-mouthed woman or foundling, no seventh hearing, no tenth stopping, no third gap, no fourth likeness made a cause, no calling of the loan, no payer named, no private record read and no ending

scenes.title: The Second Working Week
scenes.synopsis: First entry, first dated heading and drop capital: Day 183, Ember 4, Fourthday, before first grey through the opening of the kiln under the Vail roof, at the bed, the hearth, the loaf shelf's low angle, the kiln mouth and the edge of the Clay Yard. No recap of the close of Chapter 43. The boy is one hundred and eighty-three days old and six months and three days and nobody under any roof says so (T071/T072). The first smell is hot clay under tallow and wet wool with the sour mineral breath of the unswept corner; the first sound is the kiln's breath in fours with a gap, not a bell. Under the floor the carried fire answers four low pulls and the silence where the fifth should have been, its payer unnamed for a hundred and eighty-three days (T088); through the finger's-width door the river keeps its note of water over water, a fifth low thing never counted among the hearings and never invented to stand up as a seventh; overhead the boards keep four nails, four, and a knot the width of a thumb --- three counts in three places that do not become one (T061/T082). The crust lies stiff and leathery two inches from his ear with its empty place unnamed and no third, the thread of drool frozen and unwiped, his hand outside the wool going up an inch toward the note of water and coming down against the fold. Sella gives every instruction to the wool, the fire, the pot, the broom and the running water and never to the basket, says the house where another woman would say I, keeps her half-pace, glances once at the clay jar cold under its glaze and shuts her hand half over nothing without touching it, pushes coal-black hair back with the burn-wrist so the grey streak shows pale off the coals, and sets the pot rim out with its handle two inches beyond the reaching hand, her hand resting a half-beat longer at the setting (T058/T079). The widow's mark hangs where it hung, untouched, because a morning and a shelf are not openings and the one opening was before the kiln on Ember 1. The yard goes around the clean dark line, the finer grey called the thaw, the rack space with its broken birth-slates, the pan's gone round place, the bare dark trough whose water is called weather and the empty place in the returning line where a hand went in on Seed 15, with a look and a wide step and no number and no explanation given to the basket (T009/T013/T092, T098 carried). At the kiln mouth the fire keeps its gap; the coals stay banked under blind ash and a broken pot; the danger keeps an order and no name that cannot be carried into a chart --- hot clay, slate dust ground small as meal, the sweetish edge of lead glaze on a wrong wind. No payer is named, no pot is lost and no lesson made. Close on his wanting the crust, the breast, the pot handle and a number spoken by somebody who would have known what a number counted, and getting none, with one hundred and eighty-three exact and unspent in the dark of the wool.

scenes.title: The Stone in the Pot
scenes.synopsis: Second entry of Day 183, no new dated heading: afternoon into the small hours at the kindling, the flagstones, the loaf shelf, the Debt Loft above the wheel-shed, under the Vail roof and on the bed. Tarn takes the broom only after it has been given its instruction and tells the kindling Six counted. The next I don't count, with the small knife back at the very edge of its sill, six counted in the worn thumb-mark where the house can check and the seventh held at the lip where it cannot, Garl's unforged collector sentence beside it, his chest tight since the dark, Ash worked into the creases of his knuckles in the colour of the clean dark line and no scrubbing lifting it, the pale clip-ring at his left wrist holding what light there is and giving it back (T036/T076). He says Yes, house to an early thaw and a late, agrees so entirely no argument can find a foot, keeps wanting the late because it puts off the paying, sweeps the collector's road without once turning along it, and no collector comes. THE CHAPTER'S ONE MEANINGFUL CHANGE: in the Debt Loft, in the clay pot where he has kept the warm stone Sella gave him in the winter Garl died --- two years gone and cold and not looked at in a year --- he lifts the stone out, holds it, sets it on the sill where light from the finger's-width opening reaches, looks at it a long moment, and puts it back in the pot. No word, no figure, no payer, no slate. He does not reconcile it with the debt and does not forgive it; the stone stays where he put it, still cold, the change held and unspoken (T006 advanced, T036/T076 advanced, not paid). The boy, below, hears only a small dry scrape of a pot's foot set down on stone from the direction of the shed-loft, a sound from a place he cannot enter; he files it on a place of its own and does not join it to the Day 161 damper fraction, the Day 166 held beat beneath the shelf or the Day 171 flagstone half-check, and does not let a fourth likeness stand up and call itself a cause, for a rule is an account that has found a payer (T061/T082). The ear-sentence about an ear under this roof being worth more than the debt that holds it comes to his teeth and stops short of the word that would call the loan, with no figure and no name; he draws the breath he should have spent and does not spend it, no tenth stopping stands up before the seventh year is earned, the nine stay nine objects with no payer, the Seed 16 breath stays unspent at the top of every reach and the loan stays uncalled (T036/T076, T061/T082). Sella stands at the loaf shelf with her back to the basket, moves her lips along a row with two unnamed gaps, glances once at the clay jar without touching it and keeps her finger from beneath the board, so the charcoal stays unread (T100). At the going of the light she carries him home up the clay road, woodsmoke before her and river wind behind, going wide around the pan's gone place, the bare dark trough, the rack space and the field's empty place with a look and a wide step and no number (T009/T013/T092, T098); under the roof she sets him on his bed and not in the Debt Loft, puts the fold right without looking at his face, leaves the thread frozen, lets her hand rest a half-beat longer than the setting needed, tells the carried fire it was the thaw, turns the coals with the back of a broken pot, says The house will keep it, counts under her breath toward no opening, pushes coal-black hair back with the burn-wrist so the grey streak shows pale off the coals, sets the pot handle two inches beyond the reaching hand and does not look toward the bed; the widow's mark hangs where it hung, because a dusk is not an opening (T058/T079), and the two rooms do not touch. In the small hours he lays out the file as instruments on a towel: six hearings beside and never among with the sixth from a person and no seventh invented, three near-full answers advanced and not paid, nine stoppings as objects and not a rule, the three held changes on three separate places and not stood up as a rule, the loft-sill sound on a place of its own, the two shut-room tellings with no third, the told bell beside the heard, the told figure beside the paid, the shelf's two gaps, the crust's gap, the pan's gone ring and the field's empty place on trays that do not touch, with no third gap, no fourth likeness made a cause and no finger drawing the line (T061/T082, T060/T086, T065/T095). Cold arrives cheek, temple, the small bare joint at the wrist where the wool rides back, and stops; the afterdrop waits; one hundred and eighty-three stands exact and unspent; his hand goes up an inch toward the note of water and comes down against the fold.

scenes.title: The Dust Ground Small as Meal
scenes.synopsis: Third entry, third dated heading: Day 184, Ember 5, Fifthday, before first grey into the morning at the wheel-shed, the cold damper, the flagstones, the drying racks and the yard well. The boy is one hundred and eighty-four days old and six months and four days and nobody says so (T071/T072); the fire's fifth is still missing under the floor with its payer unnamed for a hundred and eighty-four days (T088). Three or four unnamed men go low into the finger's-width-open back room before first grey and get no name; Sella carries past at the half-pace, turns no head, gives the house no name for them and does not say the room is cold; the two tellings of a counting room shut in the war stand side by side with no third (T065/T095). Jorra comes through with fine grey slate dust ground small as meal into both forearms past the bent little finger and under the nails, white in the creases where a fist opened, not bone-coloured slip; he keeps dusty forearms and clean ones on one tray and asks neither which slate was broken nor whether it was a birth-slate, and the broken birth-slates stay under the lowest rack entered by nobody (T035/T031). He speaks to the wheel before anyone: It doesn't care whose hands. It cares if they're steady; tells a pot You'll do; knows its full note three turns before it leaves the wheel and withholds the knowing from a High Kiln kiln-master come up on a wrong wind, with the sweetish edge of lead glaze at one mouth-corner, who says a pot singing before its time generally sings itself out early; the knowing goes to the near-full tray beside the hearings and never among them, advanced and not paid, and no pot is lost in the yard (T061/T082). When Sella's voice goes low and unfinished at the hearth his bent finger goes to the cold iron of the damper and waits while her sentence reaches the pot, then moves the tongue a hair's breadth and leaves the finger standing; the fraction is held and unspoken, a remembered holding and not a new change, nobody speaks of the waiting and no payer is named to it, and it is not paired with the Day 166 shelf beat or the Day 171 flagstone half-check (T062). The boy reads the iron again as one piece with two bites, the holding and the taking, with no Grathic word for both mercies, filed as an object joined to no kiln (T062). Tarn's stroke goes on over the flagstones past the shallow bright patch without the half-check, so the Day 171 movement is not repeated and the three held changes stay on three separate places (T036/T076). At the yard the two unswept lines called the thaw, the rack space with its broken birth-slates, the pan's gone place, the bare dark trough whose water is called weather and the field's empty place where a hand went in on Seed 15 are gone around with a look and a wide step and no number (T009/T013/T092, T098 carried). A neighbour come up with a wet pot asks what the firing costs now the kiln month's second week is on; Sella glances once at the clay jar cold under its glaze, shuts her hand half over nothing without touching it, and sends the question to the pot and the weather with Ask the pot what a wet thing costs set down there. The house has said it; the question goes away level with nothing priced, refused or slopped (T077, T058/T079). A pot set down wrong at the racks gives its high thin note before its time and the woman who set it down does not hear it; the boy turns toward the note and gets no further and files it where a danger goes, not promoted into a near-full answer and not made a fourth likeness; no pot is lost and no lesson made (T077, T061/T082). Close on his hand going up an inch toward the river's note and coming down, with one hundred and eighty-four exact and unspent.

scenes.title: The Breath He Does Not Spend
scenes.synopsis: Fourth entry of Day 184, no new dated heading: afternoon into the small hours at the loaf shelf, the kindling, the hearth and under the Vail roof. Sella stands with her back to the basket, moving her lips along a loaf row with two unnamed gaps, gives nobody a figure, glances once at the clay jar cold under its glaze without touching it, and keeps her finger from beneath the front edge, so the charcoal tally lies unread, uncounted and uncopied and the Day 166 held beat stays where it was left (T100). At the kindling, with the coals banked and the small knife set back where it can be checked, Tarn tells the wood Six counted. The next I don't count, six in the worn thumb-mark where the house can check and the seventh at the lip where it cannot, Garl's unforged collector sentence beside it, the Seed 16 breath unspent at the top of every reach with its small interval showing where a breath should have gone in and had not. The sentence about an ear under this roof being worth more than the debt that holds it comes to his teeth and stops short of the word that would call the loan, with no figure and no name; he draws the breath he should have spent and does not spend it, says Yes, house to the fire and goes on with the broom, no tenth stopping stands up before the seventh year is earned, the nine stay nine objects with no payer named to any and the loan stays uncalled (T036/T076, T061/T082). The stone in the clay pot in the loft stays where he put it back the day before, still cold, still unreconciled with the debt by not trying, which is not forgiving; the boy files the remembered holding as a holding remembered and not a holding made again, and does not repeat it as a new change (T006 held). Sella, within hearing, gives the end of her instruction to the pot and asks nothing; Jorra does not ask about the ear and Tarn does not ask about the room, and the two silences stay unjoined. At the going of the light she carries him home up the clay road, woodsmoke going before her in long low bars and the river wind coming up behind with the taste of water over water, the two passing on the stair of the evening without taking each other's colour or spending a word on either, going wide around the pan's gone place, the bare dark trough, the rack space and the empty place in the returning line, with a look that asks for nothing and finds nothing, a wide step and no number and no explanation to the basket (T009/T013/T092, T098). Under the roof she sets him on his bed and not in the Debt Loft, base first and the weight settled the way a woman sets a vessel that must not rock, puts the fold right at his ear and under his chin without looking at his face, leaves the thread of drool frozen and unwiped because nobody under any roof has been given an instruction about the thread, lets her hand rest a half-beat longer than the setting needed, tells the carried fire it was the thaw, turns the coals with the back of a broken pot, says The house will keep it, stands a moment counting under her breath toward no opening --- the small intake at the top, the hold, the letting go --- pushes coal-black hair back with the wrist that carries the little-door burn so the grey streak shows pale off the coals, sets the pot rim out with its handle standing two inches beyond the reaching hand, and does not look toward the bed; the widow's mark hangs on its cord where it has hung since the first firing, touched once before the kiln on Ember 1 and at no shelf, well, rack, road, basket, afternoon or dusk since, because the hand goes to the mark before the kiln and at no other hour (T058/T079). The two rooms do not touch. In the small hours the file comes back exact, complete and worthless: six hearings beside and never among with no seventh, three near-full answers advanced and not paid, nine stoppings as objects and not a rule, three held changes on three separate places and not stood up as a rule, the stone's loft-sill sound on its own place, two shut-room tellings and no third, the told bell beside the heard, the told figure beside the paid, the crust's gap, the two shelf gaps, the pan's gone ring and the field's empty place on trays that do not touch, no third gap, no fourth likeness made a cause and no finger drawing the line (T061/T082, T060/T086). Close on cold at cheek, temple and the bare wrist joint, the afterdrop waiting past a warming nobody in the house will perform, his wanting the crust, the breast, the pot handle and a number spoken, and getting none, with one hundred and eighty-four exact and unspent.

scenes.title: An Order With No Name
scenes.synopsis: Fifth entry, fifth dated heading: Day 185, Ember 6, Sixthday, before first grey through the morning at the kiln mouth, the drying racks, the yard well, the flagstones and the wheel-shed edge. The boy is one hundred and eighty-five days old and six months and five days and nobody under any roof says so (T071/T072); the carried fire answers four low pulls and the silence where the fifth should have been, its payer unnamed for a hundred and eighty-five days (T088), while the river's fifth note and the boards' four nails, four and a knot keep three counts in three places that do not become another (T061/T082). The third working morning is ordinary tending and the month's danger keeps an order and no name that cannot be carried into a chart --- hot clay under tallow, fine grey slate dust ground small as meal under the nails and in the white of a knuckle when a fist opens, the sweetish edge of lead glaze on a wrong wind off High Kiln, and a pot set down wrong giving its high thin note before its time, which the woman who set it down does not hear; the boy turns toward the note and gets no further and files it as a danger of the month and not as a fourth near-full answer; no pot is lost, no lesson made and no pot singing itself out early has been paid (T077, T061/T082). The yard goes around the clean dark line, the new finer grey called the thaw, the rack space with its broken birth-slates, the pan's gone place and the field's empty place where a hand went in on Seed 15, with a look and a wide step and no number (T009/T013/T092, T098 carried). Sella gives the broom its instruction before she gives it to anybody and Tarn takes it only then, telling the wood Six counted. The next I don't count with six counted where the house can check and the seventh held where it cannot, saying Yes, house to an early thaw and a late, agreeing so entirely no argument can find a foot, keeping the late because it puts off the paying, and going over the road a house sends a man down when it wants a collector without once turning along it; no collector comes, the nine stoppings stay nine objects with no tenth before the seventh year is earned, the Seed 16 breath stays unspent, and the loan stays uncalled (T036/T076). Jorra works at the wheel with slip dried to the colour of old bone up both forearms, keeps dusty and clean forearms on one tray, tells a pot You'll do, knows its full note before it leaves the wheel and withholds it from a High Kiln voice on the wrong wind with no pot lost, and when Sella's sentence goes low his bent finger stands in the cold damper until the words reach the pot, the fraction held and unspoken, a remembered holding and not a new change, not paired with the Day 166 beat or the Day 171 flagstone half-check (T035/T031, T062). The boy reads the iron once more as one piece with two bites joined to no kiln, with no Grathic word for both mercies. Sella's eye goes once to the clay jar cold under its glaze and her hand shuts half over nothing without touching it; her finger stays from beneath the loaf shelf and the charcoal waits unread; the widow's mark hangs where it hung, because a morning and a shelf are not openings and the one opening was before the kiln on Ember 1 (T058/T079, T100). Close on the boy wanting the crust, the breast, the pot handle two inches beyond his hand and a number spoken by somebody who would have known what a number counted, and getting none, with one hundred and eighty-five exact and unspent and the fire's fifth still missing.

scenes.title: The Charcoal Waits
scenes.synopsis: Sixth entry, chapter close, no new dated heading: Day 185, Ember 6, Sixthday, afternoon into the small hours at the loaf shelf, the kindling, hearth and bed under the Vail roof and at the yard's edge of light. The afternoon thins without ending, losing its edges the way water goes off a stone that has held the sun; hot clay lies under tallow and wet wool under that, and below both the sour mineral breath of the Ash corner nobody has swept in two years. Sella stands with her back to the basket at the loaf shelf and moves her lips along a row standing with two unnamed gaps, the old space at the row's end and the palm's breadth that came in on the night of Seed 6; she gives nobody a figure, glances once at the clay jar cold under its glaze and shuts her hand half over nothing, and her finger does not go beneath the front edge, so the charcoal tally lies under the board where it has lain since the night she held a finger beneath it for one counted breath, still unread, and an afternoon and a woman's back turned are not the same as that night (T100). Tarn's knife lies on the sill of the kindling at the very edge where a man could check it and find it where it should be, six years in the worn thumb-mark where the house can put a finger and verify them, the seventh at the lip where no thumb of the house has gone, Garl's unforged collector sentence beside it, Ash worked into the creases of his knuckles in the colour of the clean dark line and no scrubbing lifting it, the pale clip-ring at his left wrist holding what light there is and giving it back; the breath from Seed 16 stands unspent at the top of every reach with its small interval where a breath should have gone in and had not, and the ear-sentence comes to his teeth and stops short of the word that would call the loan, no figure, no name, no tenth standing up before the seventh year is earned, the nine stay nine, the loan uncalled and the seventh year nearer its end than it has ever stood and not given (T036/T076, T061/T082). He says Yes, house to the fire and goes on with his work; the stone stays where he put it back in the clay pot in the loft two days gone, still cold, unreconciled by not trying, which is not forgiving, and the boy keeps the remembered holding on its own place and does not stand it up with the three held changes (T006 held). In the Vail wheel-shed Jorra works at the wheel with slip dried to the colour of old bone up both forearms and the bent little finger leading, keeps dusty forearms and clean ones on one tray and asks neither which slate was broken nor whether it was a birth-slate, speaks to the wheel before anyone (It doesn't care whose hands. It cares if they're steady), tells a pot You'll do, knows its full note three turns before it leaves the wheel and keeps the knowing back from a man come up on a wrong wind, so no pot is lost; when Sella's voice goes low and unfinished at the hearth his bent finger goes to the cold iron of the damper and waits while her sentence reaches the pot, then moves the tongue a hair's breadth and leaves the finger standing in the iron, the fraction held and unspoken and not a change made twice over; he gives the men who came before first grey no name and does not say the room is cold, and the two shut-room tellings stay two with no third (T062, T035/T031, T065/T095). At the going of the light she carries him home up the clay road, woodsmoke going before her in long low bars out of the chimneys and the river wind coming up behind with the taste of water over water, the two passing on the stair of the evening as they have passed every evening of his life without taking each other's colour or spending a word on either; the instruction goes to the wool and the river wind and never to the basket, the arm that has carried him a hundred and eighty-five mornings keeps the height of the handle and the give of the shoulder and the turn of the wrist at a step's end, a record in muscle that gives no account of the cost. At the edge of the yard she goes around the round place where the shallow clay pan had stood mouth-up to dry through Reed and is standing there no longer, around the well where the trough stands bare and dark and its water is called weather, wide around the space beneath the lowest rack where the broken birth-slates lie, and around the empty place in the returning line where a hand went in on Seed 15 and did not come out, with a look that asks for nothing and finds nothing, a wide step and no number and no explanation to the basket (T009/T013/T092, T098). Under the roof she sets him on his bed and not in the Debt Loft, base first and the weight settled the way a woman sets a vessel that must not rock, puts the fold right at his ear and under his chin without once looking at his face, leaves the thread of drool frozen and unwiped because nobody under any roof has been given an instruction about the thread, lets her hand rest a half-beat longer than the setting needed before it went away, tells the carried fire it was the thaw, turns the coals with the back of a broken pot, says The house will keep it, stands a moment with the back of the pot in her hand counting under her breath toward no opening --- the small intake at the top, the hold, the letting go --- pushes coal-black hair back with the wrist that carries the little-door burn so the grey streak shows pale off the coals, sets the pot rim out on the board with its handle standing two inches beyond the reaching hand, and does not look toward the bed. The widow's mark hangs on its cord at her throat where it has hung since the first firing; it was touched once, before the kiln on the first morning of the month, and at no shelf and no well and no afternoon and no dusk since, because a shelf and a well and an afternoon and a dusk are not openings and the hand goes to the mark before the kiln and at no other hour; the two rooms do not touch (T058/T079). In the small hours he turns out the file the way a man lays instruments on a towel before a case begins, each thing going into its own hollow and nothing resting across anything else: six hearings of the full note beside and never among --- five from four sources, a cup across a birth room, a pot in the wheel-shed through a finger's width of door, the district's slate twice at the Cross and a man giving at the Drawing --- and the sixth, the small flat knock out of Dessa Silt as the men lifted her, filed where a thing out of a person must go and never among the sources, no seventh in a hundred and eighty-five days and none invented to fill the empty place, for an empty place kept empty is a finding and a place filled to make a row come out even is a finding forged; three near-full answers on their own tray, advanced and not paid; the older intervals at Stone 13, Stone 17 and Stone 25; nine stoppings --- Reed 5, 8, 11, 14, 17, 20, 23, 26 and 29 --- objects and not a rule, intervals and not payments, no payer named to any, with a tenth not stood up before the seventh year was earned; the damper beside them as one piece of iron with two bites and no Grathic word for both mercies; three held changes on three separate places --- the fraction at the iron in a wall, the beat held beneath the loaf shelf in a room that does not touch the wall, the half-check on the flagstones in a yard that touches neither --- not a pair, not a doctrine, not a rule, for a rule is an account that has found a payer and no payer stands to any of the three, with the stone's small loft-sill sound on a fourth place of its own and not laid across them; the two tellings of a counting room shut in the war side by side with no third; the told bell kept beside the heard bell, four, four and a gap with nobody crossing himself; the told figure beside the paid; the sixth green a colour joined to no ear and the foundling a shape with no sale, offstage and unspent, and the soft-cuffed clerk still set at the out-of-line landing for a measure nobody called; the shelf's two gaps, the fold's crust and its gap, the pan's gone round ring and the empty place in the returning line on trays that do not touch, no third gap, no fourth likeness made a cause and no finger of his drawing the line, because three likenesses in a row will stand up and call themselves a truth if a man leaves them standing and he has spent a hundred and eighty-five days taking them down one at a time with nobody to help and nobody to see. Through the finger's-width door the river keeps its note of water over water, a fifth low thing never counted among the hearings; through the floor the carried fire gives four low pulls and the silence where the fifth should have been, its payer without a name for a hundred and eighty-five days; overhead the boards keep four nails, four, and a knot the width of a thumb --- three counts in three places, and none rises up and becomes the others. Ash lies thin along the skirting board in the colour of the clean dark line and the new finer grey called the thaw lies beside it, neither swept and neither with an instruction; cold comes cheek, temple, the small bare joint at the wrist where the wool rides back, and stops as if it had reached the end of its own order, the afterdrop waiting on the far side of a warming nobody in this house will perform. He wants the crust two inches from his ear, the breast, the pot handle standing two inches beyond his hand and a number spoken by somebody who would have known what a number counted, and gets none of them, and has stopped expecting to be told, which is not the same as not wanting it; the surgeon's register reads the whole as an inventory that is not a key and a list that is not a hand, exact, complete and worth nothing at two paces, and he is the only adult in the room and the least use in it. One hundred and eighty-five stands exact, complete and unspent in the dark of the wool, spoken by nobody under any roof; nothing was joined, named, opened, called, spent or ended, the fire's fifth still missing under the floor with its payer unnamed, the ninth stopping still nine, the Seed 16 breath still held, the three changes still on their three places, the mark touched once before the kiln and at no other hour, the stone back in its pot in the loft still cold and unreconciled, and the charcoal still waiting under the shelf for a hand that is not hers and a day that has not come. His hand outside the wool goes up an inch toward the note of water over water through the finger's-width door and comes down against the fold, and the count goes forward into Day 186, Ember 7.
